title.zh: 卷一百一十 列傳第六十: 李光弼 王思禮 鄧景山 辛雲京
title.en: Volume 110 Biographies 60: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Deng Jingshan, Xin Yunjing
title.raw: 卷一百一十 列傳第六十: 李光弼 王思禮 鄧景山 辛雲京 Volume 110 Biographies 60: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Deng Jingshan, Xin Yunjing

sentences.zh: 魯炅，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jiong—Lu Jiong was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiong was from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺餘，涉獵書史，

translations.literal: He stood more than seven chi in height and had dipped into books and histories,
translations.idiomatic: He was over seven chi tall and had read widely in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 天寶六年，隴右節度使哥舒翰引為別奏。

translations.literal: the Longyou military governor Geshu Han recruited him as a special memorialist.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Geshu Han, military governor of Longyou, brought him in as a special memorialist.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿為監察御史，使至隴右，翰嘗設宴，真卿謂翰曰：「中丞自郎將授將軍，便登節制，後生可畏，得無人乎？」

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing was a investigating censor; when he was sent to Longyou, Han once gave a banquet, and Zhenqing said to Han, "Your Excellency went from commandant to general and straightway rose to a frontier command—youth can be feared; are there not men [among them]?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing served as investigating censor and traveled to Longyou, Geshu Han once held a feast. Zhenqing said to him, "You rose from commandant to general and at once took a frontier command—there is much to fear in the young; surely you have capable men?

sentences.zh: 炅時立在階下，翰指炅曰：「此人後當為節度使矣。」

translations.literal: Jiong was then standing below the steps; Han pointed at Jiong and said, "This man will later become a military governor."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was standing on the steps below. Han pointed to him and said, "This man will one day be a military governor."

sentences.zh: 後以隴右破吐蕃跳蕩功，累授右領軍大將軍同正員，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in defeating the Tibetan raiders in Longyou, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Army General-in-Chief with concurrent status and was granted the purple-gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for victories over Tibetan raiders in Longyou, he rose step by step to Right Army General-in-Chief with full concurrent rank and received the purple-gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，選任將帥。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, generals were selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: With the outbreak of An Lushan's rebellion, commanders were chosen for appointment.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，拜炅上洛太守，未行，遷南陽太守、本郡守捉，仍充防禦使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Jiong was appointed Governor of Shangluo; before he set out, he was transferred to Governor of Nanyang, with charge of defending his own prefecture, and was also made defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Jiong was named Governor of Shangluo. Before he departed, he was moved to Governor of Nanyang with local defense duties and made defense commissioner as well.

sentences.zh: 尋兼御史大夫，充南陽節度使，以嶺南、黔中、山南東道子弟五萬人屯葉縣北，滍水之南，築柵，四面掘壕以自固。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made Censor-in-Chief and Nanyang military governor; with fifty thousand youths from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Shannan East Circuit he encamped north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built palisades, and dug moats on all sides to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the concurrent title Censor-in-Chief and made Nanyang military governor. He stationed fifty thousand troops from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Shannan East north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built stockades, and dug trenches on every side to hold his position.

sentences.zh: 至五月，賊將武令珣、畢思琛等來擊之，眾欲出戰，炅不許。

translations.literal: By the fifth month, the rebel generals Wu Lingxun, Bi Sichen, and others came to attack; the troops wished to go out and fight, but Jiong would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, rebel generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked. The men wanted to give battle, but Jiong refused.

sentences.zh: 賊於營西順風燒煙，營內坐立不得，橫門扇及木爭出，賊矢集如雨，炅與中使薛道等挺身遁走，余眾盡沒。

translations.literal: The rebels burned smoke upwind on the west of the camp; inside the camp men could neither sit nor stand; they rushed the side gates and timbers to get out; rebel arrows fell like rain; Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others fled headlong, and the rest of the force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set smoke to windward west of the camp until the troops could neither sit nor stand. They surged through the side gates and over the timbers; arrows fell like rain. Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others bolted, and the remainder of the army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、襄陽太守徐浩未至，裨將嶺南、黔中、荊襄子弟半在軍，多懷金銀為資糧，軍資器械盡棄於路如山積。

translations.literal: The Lingnan military governor He Lüguang, the Qianzhong military governor Zhao Guozhen, and the Xiangyang prefect Xu Hao had not yet arrived; half the subordinate officers and youths of Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jing-Xiang were in the army; many carried gold and silver as provisions; military stores and weapons were abandoned along the road in heaps like hills.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan governor He Lüguang, Qianzhong governor Zhao Guozhen, and Xiangyang prefect Xu Hao had not yet come up. Half the subordinate officers from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jing-Xiang were in the ranks, many laden with gold and silver for supplies. Arms and equipment were cast aside along the road in mountain-high piles.

sentences.zh: 至是賊徒不勝其富。

translations.literal: At this the rebels could scarcely carry off such wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could hardly carry away such riches.

sentences.zh: 炅收合殘卒，保南陽郡，為賊所圍。

translations.literal: Jiong gathered the broken remnants and held Nanyang Prefecture, and was besieged by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong rallied the survivors, held Nanyang, and was surrounded by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尋而潼關失守，賊使哥舒翰招之，不從。

translations.literal: Before long Tong Pass fell; the rebels sent Geshu Han to summon him, but he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Tong Pass fell, the rebels sent Geshu Han to win him over, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 又使偽將豫州刺史武令珣等攻之，累月不能克。

translations.literal: They again sent the false general and Yuzhou prefect Wu Lingxun and others to attack him; for many months they could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent the puppet Yuzhou prefect Wu Lingxun and others against him; for months they could not capture the city.

sentences.zh: 武令珣死，又令田承嗣攻之。

translations.literal: When Wu Lingxun died, they ordered Tian Chengsi to attack.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Lingxun died, Tian Chengsi was ordered to press the siege.

sentences.zh: 潁川太守來瑱、襄陽太守魏仲犀合勢救之。

translations.literal: The Yingchuan prefect Lai Zhen and the Xiangyang prefect Wei Zhongxi joined forces to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan prefect Lai Zhen and Xiangyang prefect Wei Zhongxi combined their forces to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 犀使弟孟馴為將，領兵至明府橋，望賊而走，眾遂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhongxi sent his younger brother Mengxun as commander; leading troops to Mingfu Bridge, he fled at sight of the rebels, and the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi put his brother Mengxun in command. Mengxun led troops to Mingfu Bridge, fled at sight of the enemy, and the force was routed.

sentences.zh: 炅城中食盡，煮牛皮筋角而食之，米鬥至四五十千，有價無米，鼠一頭至四百文，餓死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: Food in Jiong's city was exhausted; they boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn to eat; a dou of rice reached forty or fifty thousand cash—there was a price but no grain; a single rat fetched four hundred cash; the starved lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions in the city ran out. The defenders boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn to eat. A dou of rice cost forty or fifty thousand cash—money without grain to buy. A rat sold for four hundred cash. The dead from hunger lay heaped together.

sentences.zh: 肅宗使中官將軍曹日昇來宣慰，路絕不得入。

translations.literal: Suzong sent the palace general Cao Risheng to proclaim comfort; the roads were cut and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong sent the palace general Cao Risheng with imperial comfort, but the routes were blocked and he could not get in.

sentences.zh: 日昇請單騎入致命，仲犀曰：「不可，賊若擒吾敕使，我亦何安！」

translations.literal: Risheng asked to enter alone to deliver the charge; Zhongxi said, "It cannot be done—if the rebels seize our imperial envoy, how shall I stand secure!"
translations.idiomatic: Risheng asked to ride in alone with the imperial message. Zhongxi said, "That cannot be—if the rebels seize our envoy, how can I answer for it?

sentences.zh: 顏真卿適自河北次於襄陽，謂仲犀曰：「曹使既果決，不顧萬死之地，何得沮之！

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing happened to be stopping in Xiangyang on his way from Hebei and said to Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is so resolute that he does not shrink from a place of ten thousand deaths—how can you discourage him!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, just arrived in Xiangyang from Hebei, told Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is so determined that he does not fear death itself—how can you hold him back?

sentences.zh: 縱為賊所獲，是亡一使者；

translations.literal: Even if he were taken by the rebels, that would be the loss of one envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Even if the rebels seized him, that would mean only one envoy lost;

sentences.zh: 敬得入城，則萬人之心固矣。

translations.literal: if respectfully he can enter the city, then the hearts of ten thousand men will be made firm.
translations.idiomatic: but if he reaches the city, the hearts of ten thousand men will be secured.

sentences.zh: 公何愛焉？」

translations.literal: Why do you begrudge him?"
translations.idiomatic: Why begrudge him the attempt?"

sentences.zh: 中官馮廷環曰：「將軍必能入，我請以兩騎助之。」

translations.literal: The palace official Feng Tinghuan said, "The general can surely get in; I ask to assist him with two horsemen."
translations.idiomatic: The palace official Feng Tinghuan said, "The general can surely enter; let me lend two horsemen."

sentences.zh: 日昇又自有傔騎數人，仲犀又以數騎共十人同行。

translations.literal: Risheng also had several personal riders; Zhongxi added several more—ten men in all went together.
translations.idiomatic: Risheng had his own attendants as well; Zhongxi added several riders, and ten men went in together.

sentences.zh: 賊徒望見，知其驍銳，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The rebels saw them from afar, knew them for fierce fighters, and did not press them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw them from afar, knew them for fierce men, and did not close in.

sentences.zh: 日昇既入城，炅眾初以為望絕，忽有使來宣命，皆踴躍一心。

translations.literal: Once Risheng had entered the city, Jiong's troops had at first thought all hope gone; suddenly an envoy came bearing the imperial charge, and all leapt up with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Risheng entered the city, Jiong's men had thought themselves forsaken. Suddenly an envoy arrived with the imperial message, and they rallied as one.

sentences.zh: 日昇以其十人至襄陽取糧，賊雖追之，不敢擊，遂以一千人取音聲路運糧而入，賊亦不能遏，又得相持數月。

translations.literal: Risheng took his ten men to Xiangyang to fetch grain; though the rebels pursued, they did not attack; then with a thousand men he took the Yinsheng route to bring grain in; the rebels could not stop him either, and they were able to hold out several months more.
translations.idiomatic: Risheng led his ten men to Xiangyang for grain. The rebels pursued but dared not attack. He then sent a thousand men along the Yinsheng route to convoy grain into the city; the rebels could not block them, and the siege dragged on for months more.

sentences.zh: 炅在圍中一年，救兵不至，晝夜苦戰，人相食。

translations.literal: Jiong was besieged for a year; relief did not come; day and night they fought bitterly; men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong remained under siege for a year. No relief arrived. Day and night the fighting was desperate, and men ate one another.

sentences.zh: 至德二年五月十五日，率眾持滿傳矢突圍而出南陽，投襄陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, on the fifteenth day of the fifth month he led the masses, bows strung and arrows passed along, to burst the encirclement and break out of Nanyang, and threw himself on Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide, on the fifteenth of the fifth month he led his men, bows fully drawn and arrows at the ready, in a breakout from Nanyang and made for Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣來追，苦戰二日，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi came in pursuit; for two days they fought bitterly and killed many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi pursued. For two days they fought fiercely and killed a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊又知其決死，遂不敢逼，朝廷因除御史大夫、襄陽節度使。

translations.literal: The rebels again knew their resolve to die and did not press them; the court thereupon appointed him Censor-in-Chief and Xiangyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing their willingness to die to the last man, the rebels dared not close in. The court then appointed him Censor-in-Chief and military governor of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 時賊志欲南侵江、漢，賴炅奮命扼其沖要，南夏所以保全。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels intended to push south into the Yangzi and Han regions; it was by Jiong's desperate defense of the strategic choke point that South China was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then meant to drive south into the Yangzi and Han valleys. Jiong's desperate stand at the vital pass is what kept the south intact.

sentences.zh: 十月，王師收兩京，承嗣、令珣等奔於河北。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the imperial army recovered the two capitals; Chengsi, Lingxun, and others fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the imperial forces retook the two capitals. Chengsi, Lingxun, and others fled to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 南陽遭大亂之後，距鄧州二百里，人煙斷絕，遺骸委積於墻塹間。

translations.literal: After the great disorder at Nanyang, for two hundred li toward Dengzhou human habitation ceased; corpses lay heaped between walls and ditches.
translations.idiomatic: After the catastrophe at Nanyang, for two hundred li toward Dengzhou not a soul was to be seen; bones and bodies lay piled in the ruins.

sentences.zh: 十二月，策勛行賞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month merit was assessed and rewards distributed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month achievements were tallied and rewards granted.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「特進、太僕卿、南陽郡守、兼御史大夫、權知襄陽節度事、上柱國、金鄉縣公魯炅，蘊是韜略，副茲節制，竭節保邦，悉心陷敵。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Special Grand Master of the Palace, Minister of the Imperial Stud, Governor of Nanyang, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, acting Xiangyang military governor, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Jinxiang County Lu Jiong—he possesses strategy, assists this command, exhausts loyalty to preserve the realm, and devotes his heart to striking the foe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Lu Jiong, Special Grand Master of the Palace, Minister of the Imperial Stud, Governor of Nanyang, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, acting Xiangyang military governor, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Jinxiang, is versed in strategy, faithful in command, and has exhausted himself to defend the state and throw himself against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 表之旗幟，分以土田。

translations.literal: Let his banners be displayed and lands allotted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Let his banners be raised and lands granted him.

sentences.zh: 可開府儀同三司、兼御史大夫，封岐國公，食實封二百戶，兼京兆尹。」，

translations.literal: He may be made Grand General with the insignia of a chief minister, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Qi, with an estate of two hundred households, and also Governor of Jingzhao.",
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand General with chief-minister insignia, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Duke of Qi with an estate of two hundred households, and Governor of Jingzhao."

sentences.zh: 兼鄭州刺史，充鄭、陳、潁、亳等州節度使，

translations.literal: and also Governor of Zhengzhou, and made military governor of Zheng, Chen, Ying, Bo, and other prefectures,
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Governor of Zhengzhou and military governor over Zheng, Chen, Ying, Bo, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 為淮西襄陽節度使、鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: and was made Huai-Xi and Xiangyang military governor and Governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Huai-Xi and Xiangyang and Governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，與朔方節度使司徒郭子儀、河東節度使太尉李光弼等九節度同圍安慶緒於相州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, together with the Shuofang military governor and Minister of Works Guo Ziyi, the Hedong military governor and Grand Marshal Li Guangbi, and eight other frontier commands, he jointly besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined Shuofang governor Guo Ziyi, Hedong governor Li Guangbi, and eight other commanders in besieging An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 炅領淮西、襄陽節度行營步卒萬人、馬軍三百，以李抱玉為兵馬使，炅分界知東面之北。

translations.literal: Jiong led ten thousand infantry and three hundred cavalry of the Huai-Xi and Xiangyang campaign army; Li Baoyu was made army commander; Jiong's sector was the north of the eastern face.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong commanded ten thousand foot soldiers and three hundred horsemen of the Huai-Xi–Xiangyang field army, with Li Baoyu as army commander. His sector lay on the north of the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 二年六月六日，賊將史思明自范陽來救，戰於安陽河北，王師不利，炅中流矢奔退。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, the rebel general Shi Siming came from Fanyang to relieve the city; they fought north of Anyang on the Yellow River; the imperial army was at a disadvantage; Jiong was struck by an arrow and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year, Shi Siming marched from Fanyang to relieve the siege. The armies clashed north of Anyang on the Yellow River. The imperial side faltered; Jiong took an arrow wound and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時諸節度以回紇戰敗，因而退散，盡棄軍糧器械，所過虜掠，炅兵士剽奪尤甚，人因驚怨。

translations.literal: At that time the various commands, because the Uyghurs had been defeated, thereupon dispersed; they abandoned all grain and weapons; wherever they passed they plundered; Jiong's soldiers looted worst of all, and the people were shocked and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghur allies were beaten, the commanders broke up, cast away grain and arms, and plundered every district they crossed. Jiong's troops pillaged worst of all, and popular resentment flared.

sentences.zh: 五日，至新鄭縣，聞郭子儀已整眾屯谷水，李光弼還太原，炅憂懼，仰藥而卒。

translations.literal: On the fifth day, reaching Xinzheng County, he heard that Guo Ziyi had already reassembled his force at Gushui and Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan; Jiong, anxious and afraid, took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth he reached Xinzheng and learned that Guo Ziyi had regrouped at Gushui while Li Guangbi had gone back to Taiyuan. In fear and despair Jiong took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 裴裴，以門廕入仕，累遷京兆府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: Pei Ying—Pei Ying entered office through hereditary privilege and was promoted repeatedly to Recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying entered government by yin privilege and rose to Recorder of the Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 來瑱鎮陜州，引為判官；

translations.literal: When Lai Zhen governed Shaanzhou, he was brought in as aide;
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Zhen was posted to Shaanzhou, Ying served as his aide;

sentences.zh: 瑱移襄州，又為瑱行軍司馬，瑱遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: when Zhen moved to Xiangzhou, he again became Zhen's campaign secretary; Zhen treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhen moved to Xiangzhou, Ying became his campaign secretary, and Zhen favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及瑱淮西之敗，逗留不行，密表聞奏。

translations.literal: When Zhen was defeated in Huai-Xi, Ying lingered and did not go; he memorialized the throne in secret.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's defeat in Huai-Xi, Ying stayed behind and secretly reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以瑱掌重兵，惡之，密詔以代瑱為襄州刺史，充防禦使。

translations.literal: The court, because Zhen held great military power, disliked him, and by secret edict appointed Ying to replace Zhen as Governor of Xiangzhou and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court, uneasy that Zhen commanded so large an army, secretly ordered Ying to replace him as Governor of Xiangzhou and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 本鎮谷城，及受密命，乃率麾下二千人赴襄陽。

translations.literal: Ying's original post was Gucheng; on receiving the secret order he led two thousand men under his command to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had governed Gucheng; on receiving the secret commission he led two thousand of his men to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 時瑱亦奉詔依舊任，瑱遂設具於江津以俟之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen also had an edict confirming him in his former post; Zhen thereupon set out a feast on the river ford to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen too had orders to keep his post. He laid a feast at the river crossing to receive Ying.

sentences.zh: 初聲言假道入朝，及見瑱，即雲奉代，且欲視事。

translations.literal: At first Ying claimed he was only passing through on his way to court; when he met Zhen he at once said he had come to replace him and wished to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ying said he was merely passing through on his way to the capital; when he met Zhen he declared that he had come to replace him and meant to assume command.

sentences.zh: 瑱報曰：「瑱已奉恩命復任此。」

translations.literal: Zhen replied, "Zhen has already received the gracious order to resume this post."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen answered, "I have already received the gracious order to remain in this post.

sentences.zh: 惶惑，喻其麾下曰：「此言必妄。」

translations.literal: Ying, alarmed, told his followers, "These words must be false."
translations.idiomatic: Ying, shaken, told his men, "That cannot be true."

sentences.zh: 遂引射瑱軍，因與瑱兵交戰，大敗，士卒死傷殆盡。

translations.literal: He thereupon drew his bow and shot at Zhen's army; he joined battle with Zhen's troops, was utterly defeated, and his soldiers were nearly all killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his bow on Zhen's troops and joined battle. Ying was routed; his men were almost annihilated.

sentences.zh: 走還谷城舊營，瑱追擒之。

translations.literal: Ying fled back to his old camp at Gucheng; Zhen pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying fled to his old camp at Gucheng; Zhen pursued and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 朝旨務安漢南，乃歸咎於。

translations.literal: The court's intent was to pacify the Han south; blame was therefore laid on Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to settle the Han south in peace, so the fault was pinned on Ying.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年七月，敕曰：「前襄州刺史裴，性本頑疏，行惟狂悖。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Baoying an edict said: "Former Governor of Xiangzhou Pei Ying is by nature crude and shallow, and in conduct wildly perverse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Baoying 762 an edict declared: "The former Governor of Xiangzhou, Pei Ying, is coarse by nature and reckless in conduct.

sentences.zh: 頃因試用，爰委軍戎，守在要沖，無聞方略。

translations.literal: Recently, on trial appointment, military affairs were entrusted to him; he guarded a vital point but showed no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, on probation, he was entrusted with military affairs at a critical post, yet showed no capacity for command.

sentences.zh: 所以申命來瑱，重撫漢南，即宜奔赴闕廷，謝其曠職。

translations.literal: Therefore orders were sent to Lai Zhen to reassure the Han south anew; he should at once hurry to court and answer for his neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen was therefore ordered to reassure the Han south; Ying should have hurried to court to answer for his neglect.

sentences.zh: 而乃顧惜名位，輕圖異端，誣構忠良，妄興兵甲。

translations.literal: Yet he clung to rank and title, lightly plotted sedition, slandered the loyal, and rashly raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he clung to office, plotted rebellion, slandered loyal men, and rashly took up arms.

sentences.zh: 遽令追召，敢欲逗留，是有無君之心，不唯罔上之罪。

translations.literal: When he was suddenly summoned to return, he dared to linger—this is a heart without a ruler, not merely the crime of deceiving one's superiors.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he dared to delay—this is disloyalty itself, not merely deceit toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 又轉輸之物，軍國所資，擅為費用，其數甚廣。

translations.literal: Moreover the goods of transport, the resources of army and state, he expended on his own authority in very great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He also misappropriated vast stores meant for army and state.

sentences.zh: 據其抵犯，合置嚴誅。

translations.literal: Judging his offenses, he deserves stern execution.
translations.idiomatic: By his crimes he deserves death.

sentences.zh: 但自朕登極已來，屢施恩宥，肆諸朝市，所未忍為。

translations.literal: But since We ascended the throne We have repeatedly shown mercy; to display him in the marketplace We have not yet been willing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Our accession We have often shown mercy and are unwilling to execute him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 宜寬殊死之刑，俾就投荒之謫，宜除名，長流費州。」

translations.literal: Let the penalty of death be commuted; let him be sent into exile in the wilds; let his name be struck from the rolls and let him be banished far to Feizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Let the death penalty be spared; let him be stripped of name and office and banished to Feizhou."

sentences.zh: 器局輕褊，初興師徒，給用無節。

translations.literal: Ying was light and narrow in temperament; when he first raised troops his supplies were without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was shallow and petty. When he first took the field he spent without restraint.

sentences.zh: 及敗撓，遲回赴召，將至京師，會有是命。

translations.literal: When he was defeated and shaken, he delayed in answering the summons; as he was about to reach the capital, this order overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat he lingered on the road to court; just as he neared the capital, the edict caught up with him.

sentences.zh: 既行，至藍田驛，賜自盡。

translations.literal: He had already set out; reaching Lantian Post, he was granted death by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He had already started south; at Lantian Post he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 來瑱，邠州永壽人也。

translations.literal: Lai Zhen—Lai Zhen was a native of Yongshou in Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen was from Yongshou in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 父曜，起於卒伍，

translations.literal: His father Yao rose from the ranks,
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao had risen from common soldiery.

sentences.zh: 為鴻臚卿同正員、安西副都護、持節磧西副大使、四鎮節度使，後為右領軍大將軍、仗內五坊等使，名著西陲，

translations.literal: and served as Minister of State Ceremonies with concurrent status, Vice Protector-General of Anxi, Vice Commissioner with staff for the Western Regions, and military governor of the Four Garrisons; later he was Right Army General-in-Chief and director of the Five Stables within the palace guard; his fame stood on the western frontier,
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan he became Minister of State Ceremonies with concurrent status, Vice Protector-General of Anxi, commissioner for the Western Regions, and military governor of the Four Garrisons; later he was Right Army General-in-Chief and director of the Five Stables in the inner guard—famed across the western marches.

sentences.zh: 以子貴，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: and because of his son's eminence was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, because of his son's rank, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 瑱少尚名節，慷慨有大志，頗涉書傳。

translations.literal: Zhen in youth prized honor; he was generous and had great aims; he dipped considerably into books and traditions.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhen prized integrity, was bold and ambitious, and read widely.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，四鎮從職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he followed service in the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he served in the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 十一載，為左贊善大夫、殿中侍御史，充伊西、北庭行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Palace Censor, and campaign secretary for Yixi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, palace censor, and campaign secretary for Yixi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔朝臣舉智謀果決、才堪統眾者各一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered the court ministers each to recommend one man of wisdom, resolute counsel, and talent fit to command the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered each court minister to recommend one man wise, resolute, and fit to command troops.

sentences.zh: 拾遺張鎬薦瑱有縱橫之略，臨事能斷，堪當禦悔之任。

translations.literal: The remonstrance official Zhang Hao recommended Zhen as having stratagems of alliance and opposition, able to decide affairs on the spot, fit for the task of warding off regret.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Zhang Hao recommended Zhen for strategic breadth, decisiveness in crisis, and fitness to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was praised for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，張垍復薦之，起復兼汝南郡太守，未行，改潁川太守。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Zhang Ya again recommended him; he was recalled from mourning to be concurrent Governor of Runan; before he set out he was changed to Governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose, Zhang Ya recommended him again. Recalled from mourning, he was named concurrent Governor of Runan; before he departed he was shifted to Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 賊攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked the city.

sentences.zh: 城中積粟素多，瑱繕修有備。

translations.literal: Stored grain in the city had always been abundant; Zhen repaired and prepared defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The city held large stores of grain; Zhen strengthened its defenses.

sentences.zh: 賊繼至城下，瑱親射之，無不應弦而斃。

translations.literal: The rebels came in succession beneath the walls; Zhen shot them in person; none failed to fall at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns came up to the walls; Zhen shot in person, and none escaped the bowstring.

sentences.zh: 賊使降將畢思琛招瑱，琛即瑱父曜故將，城下拜泣吊瑱，瑱不應。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the surrendered general Bi Sichen to summon Zhen; Sichen had been an old officer of Zhen's father Yao; below the wall he bowed and wept in mourning for Zhen; Zhen did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the defector Bi Sichen to win him over. Sichen had served Zhen's father Yao; below the wall he bowed and wept as at a funeral. Zhen would not reply.

sentences.zh: 前後殺賊頗眾，鹹呼瑱為「來嚼鐵」。

translations.literal: Before and after he killed many rebels; all called Zhen "Lai Chews Iron."
translations.idiomatic: He killed many rebels in the fighting, and men nicknamed him "Lai Chews Iron."

sentences.zh: 以功加銀青光祿大夫，攝御史中丞、本郡防禦使及河南淮南遊奕逐要招討等使。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, acting Censor-in-Chief, defense commissioner of his own prefecture, and the Henan, Huainan, Patrol, Pursuit, and Recruitment commissioner, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, acting Censor-in-Chief, prefectural defense commissioner, and commissioner for Henan and Huainan patrol and pursuit forces, among other titles.

sentences.zh: 魯炅敗於葉縣，退守南陽，乃以瑱為南陽太守、兼御史中丞，充山南東道節度防禦處置等使以代炅。

translations.literal: When Lu Jiong was defeated at Ye County and withdrew to hold Nanyang, Zhen was made Governor of Nanyang, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East frontier defense and disposal commissioner to replace Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Jiong's defeat at Ye and withdrawal to Nanyang, Zhen was made Governor of Nanyang, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East defense commissioner in his place.

sentences.zh: 尋以嗣虢王巨為御史大夫、河南節度使，因奏炅守南陽，詔各復本位。

translations.literal: Soon the heir Prince of Guo was made Censor-in-Chief and Henan military governor; he memorialized that Jiong should hold Nanyang; an edict restored each to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Guo was made Censor-in-Chief and Henan military governor; he urged that Jiong keep Nanyang, and an edict returned each man to his former post.

sentences.zh: 賊攻圍南陽累月，瑱分兵與襄陽節度使魏仲犀救之。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged Nanyang for many months; Zhen divided his force with the Xiangyang military governor Wei Zhongxi to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged Nanyang for months. Zhen detached troops with Xiangyang governor Wei Zhongxi to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 犀遣弟孟馴將兵至明府橋，望風敗走，賊追蹙，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Zhongxi sent his younger brother Mengxun as general; leading troops to Mingfu Bridge, he fled at sight of the wind and was pressed by the rebels; he returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi sent his brother Mengxun to Mingfu Bridge; he broke at the first alarm, was chased down, and returned in rout.

sentences.zh: 兵素少，遇敗，人情恟懼，瑱綏撫訓練，賊不能侵。

translations.literal: The troops had always been few; meeting defeat, the people's hearts were fearful; Zhen pacified and trained them, and the rebels could not break in.
translations.idiomatic: His force had always been small; after the defeat panic spread, but Zhen steadied and drilled the men, and the rebels could not penetrate.

sentences.zh: 詔為淮南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was ordered made Huainan West Circuit military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Huainan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 收復兩京，與魯炅同制加開府儀同三司、兼御史大夫，封潁國公，食實封二百戶，余如故，

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, by the same edict as Lu Jiong he was promoted to Grand General with chief-minister insignia, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Ying with an estate of two hundred households; the rest remained as before,
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were retaken, he received the same promotion as Lu Jiong: Grand General with chief-minister insignia, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Duke of Ying with an estate of two hundred households; his other titles stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，召為殿中監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, he was summoned to be Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan, He was summoned to serve as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 二年，初除涼州刺史、河南節度經略副大使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was first appointed Governor of Liangzhou and deputy frontier commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was first named Governor of Liangzhou and deputy frontier commissioner for Henan.

sentences.zh: 未行，屬相州官軍為史思明所敗，東京震駭。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the Xiangzhou imperial army was defeated by Shi Siming, and the Eastern Capital was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, the imperial army at Xiangzhou was beaten by Shi Siming, and the Eastern Capital trembled.

sentences.zh: 元帥司徒郭子儀鎮谷水，乃以瑱為陜州刺史，充陜、虢等州節度，並潼關防禦、團練、鎮守使。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Guo Ziyi held Gushui; Zhen was then made Governor of Shaanzhou, military governor of Shaan and Guo, and defense, training, and garrison commissioner of Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Guo Ziyi held Gushui; Zhen was made Governor of Shaanzhou, military governor of Shaan and Guo, and defense commissioner of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年四月十三日，襄州軍將張維瑾、曹玠率眾謀亂，殺刺史史翙。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month of the third year of Qianyuan, the Xiangzhou officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie led the troops in plotting mutiny and killed the prefect Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of the fourth month of Qianyuan 760, Xiangzhou officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie mutinied and killed Prefect Shi Hui.

sentences.zh: 以瑱為襄州刺史、兼御史大夫，充山南東道襄、鄧、均、房、金、商、隨、郢、復十州節度觀察處置使，

translations.literal: Zhen was made Governor of Xiangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East military governor and disposal commissioner over ten prefectures: Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, Fu, and Fu,
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of ten Shannan East prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上元三年，肅宗召瑱入京。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan, Suzong summoned Zhen to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan, Suzong then summoned Zhen to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑱樂襄州，將士亦慕瑱之政，因諷將吏、州牧、縣宰上表請留之，身赴詔命，行及鄧州，復詔歸鎮。

translations.literal: Zhen loved Xiangzhou; the soldiers also admired his rule; he therefore prompted officers, clerks, prefects, and magistrates to memorialize asking that he be kept; he himself went to answer the summons, and when he reached Dengzhou another edict sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen loved Xiangzhou and his men admired his rule. He induced officers and local officials to petition that he remain, while he himself set out to obey the summons. At Dengzhou a new edict sent him back.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞其計而惡之。

translations.literal: Suzong heard of the scheme and disliked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong learned of the maneuver and resented it.

sentences.zh: 後呂諲、王仲昇及中官皆言瑱布恩惠，懼其得士心，以瑱為鄧州刺史，充山南東道襄、鄧、唐、復、郢、隨等六州節度，余並如故。

translations.literal: Later Lü Shen, Wang Zhongsheng, and the palace officials all said Zhen spread favors and that they feared he was winning the troops' hearts; Zhen was made Governor of Dengzhou, Shannan East military governor over six prefectures—Xiang, Deng, Tang, Fu, Ying, and Sui—the rest remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Shen, Wang Zhongsheng, and the eunuchs said Zhen was buying loyalty and might win the army's devotion. He was shifted to Dengzhou and given six prefectures; other titles stood.

sentences.zh: 俄而淮西節度王仲昇與賊將謝欽讓戰於申州城下，為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Before long the Huai-Xi military governor Wang Zhongsheng fought the rebel general Xie Qinrang below Shenzhou city and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai-Xi governor Wang Zhongsheng fought rebel general Xie Qinrang below Shenzhou and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，仲昇被圍累月，呂諲病於江陵，瑱在襄州，又恐仲昇構己，遂顧望不救。

translations.literal: At first Zhongsheng had been besieged many months; Lü Shen was ill at Jiangling; Zhen was at Xiangzhou; he also feared Zhongsheng would scheme against him, and therefore hesitated and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsheng had been besieged for months. Lü Shen lay ill at Jiangling; Zhen at Xiangzhou feared a plot against himself and held back from relief.

sentences.zh: 及師出，仲昇已沒。

translations.literal: By the time the army went out, Zhongsheng had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: When troops finally marched, Zhongsheng was already dead.

sentences.zh: 裴頻表陳瑱之狀，謀奪其位，稱「瑱善謀而勇，崛強難制，宜早除之，可一戰而擒也。」

translations.literal: Pei Ying repeatedly memorialized describing Zhen's conduct, plotting to seize his post, saying, "Zhen is skilled in planning and brave, stubborn and hard to control; he should be removed early; he can be taken in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying repeatedly reported on Zhen, scheming for his post: "Zhen is clever and fierce, proud and hard to control; remove him early and he can be seized in one battle.

sentences.zh: 肅宗然之，遂以瑱檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫、安州刺史，充淮西申、安、蘄、黃、光、沔節度觀察，兼河南陳、豫、許、鄭、汴、曹、宋、潁、泗十五州節度觀察使，外示尊崇，實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Suzong agreed; Zhen was made acting Minister of Revenue, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Anzhou, Huai-Xi observer over Shen, An, Qi, Huang, Guang, and Mian, and Henan military governor over fifteen prefectures—a show of honor that in fact stripped his power.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong agreed. Zhen was named acting Minister of Revenue with broad titular commands over Huai-Xi and Henan—honor on paper that stripped his real authority.

sentences.zh: 加裴兼御史中丞、襄鄧等七州防禦使以代之。

translations.literal: Pei Ying was also made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and defense commissioner of Xiang, Deng, and seven other prefectures to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying was made concurrent Censor-in-Chief and defense commissioner of Xiang, Deng, and seven prefectures in his stead.

sentences.zh: 瑱懼不自安，上表稱「淮西無糧饋軍，臣去秋種得麥，請待收麥畢赴上」，復諷屬吏請留之。

translations.literal: Zhen, fearful and ill at ease, memorialized, "Huai-Xi has no grain to feed the army; I sowed wheat last autumn and ask to wait until the harvest before proceeding to court," and again prompted subordinates to ask that he remain.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Zhen wrote that Huai-Xi lacked grain, that he had sown wheat the previous autumn, and begged to wait for harvest before going to court—while again prompting locals to petition for his stay.

sentences.zh: 裴於商州召募，以窺去就。

translations.literal: Pei Ying recruited troops at Shangzhou to watch whether he would go or stay.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying raised troops at Shangzhou to watch whether Zhen would go or stay.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月，代宗即位，因復授瑱襄州節度、奉義軍渭北兵馬等使，官如故，潛令裴圖之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, in the fifth month Daizong ascended the throne; Zhen was therefore reappointed Xiangzhou military governor and Fengyi Army commander north of the Wei, his offices as before; Pei Ying was secretly ordered to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, in the fifth month Emperor Daizong succeeded; Zhen was restored to Xiangzhou and the Fengyi command, while Pei Ying was secretly told to move against him.

sentences.zh: 其月十九日，裴率眾浮漢江而下。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth of that month Pei led his troops down the Han River by boat.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth Pei led his force down the Han by boat.

sentences.zh: 日暮，候者白瑱，謀於帳下，副使薛南陽曰：「尚書奉詔留鎮，裴以兵代，是無名也。

translations.literal: At dusk scouts reported to Zhen; they took counsel in the tent; the vice commissioner Xue Nanyang said, "The Minister holds the edict to remain in command; Pei comes with troops to replace him—this has no proper name.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk scouts warned Zhen. Vice commissioner Xue Nanyang said in council, "You hold the edict to remain; Pei comes with an army to replace you—this is unlawful.

sentences.zh: 且之智勇，非尚書敵也，眾心歸尚書，不歸於。

translations.literal: Moreover Ying's wisdom and courage are no match for the Minister's; the men's hearts turn to the Minister, not to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's wit and courage are no match for yours; the troops follow you, not him.

sentences.zh: 彼若乘我之不虞，今夕而至，直燒城市，我眾必懼而亂，彼乘亂而擊，則可憂也。

translations.literal: If he should take us unawares and arrive tonight, burn the city straightway—our masses will surely panic and fall into disorder; he will strike in the disorder, and then there is cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: If he surprises us tonight and fires the city, panic will break the ranks; he will strike in the chaos—that is what we must fear.

sentences.zh: 若及明而至，尚書破之必矣。」

translations.literal: If he waits until dawn to arrive, the Minister is certain to defeat him."
translations.idiomatic: If he waits until daylight, you are sure to beat him.

sentences.zh: 翌日平明，督軍士五千列於谷水北，瑱以兵逆之，登高而陣，呼將士告之曰：「爾何事來？」

translations.literal: The next day at first light he drilled five thousand soldiers drawn up north of Gushui; Zhen met the army with his troops, took a height, and formed battle lines; he called to the officers and men and said, "For what affair have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he formed five thousand men north of Gushui. Zhen drew up on high ground and shouted, "Why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「尚書不受命，謹奉中丞伐罪人。

translations.literal: They said, "The Minister does not accept the command; we respectfully follow the Vice Censor to punish the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "You refuse the command; we follow the Vice Censor to punish the offender.

sentences.zh: 若尚書受替，謹當釋兵。」

translations.literal: If the Minister accepts replacement, we will at once lay down arms."
translations.idiomatic: If you accept replacement, we will disarm at once."

sentences.zh: 瑱曰：「恩制復除瑱此州。」

translations.literal: Zhen said, "By gracious edict I am again appointed to this prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "By gracious edict I am restored to this post."

sentences.zh: 及取告身敕書以示，軍皆曰：「偽也。

translations.literal: He took out his commission and edict to show them; the army all said, "They are false.
translations.idiomatic: He produced his commission and edict; the men cried, "Forged!

sentences.zh: 承命討君，豈千里空歸，富貴在於今日。」

translations.literal: We received orders to punish you—how can we return a thousand li empty-handed? Wealth and honor lie in today."
translations.idiomatic: We were ordered to punish you—shall we march a thousand li for nothing? Fortune is here today."

sentences.zh: 遂爭射之。

translations.literal: They thereupon vied to shoot at him.
translations.idiomatic: They loosed arrows at him in a rush.

sentences.zh: 瑱奔歸旗下，薛南陽曰：「事急矣，請以三百騎為奇兵，尚書勿與之戰。」

translations.literal: Zhen ran back beneath his banners; Xue Nanyang said, "The affair is urgent; let three hundred cavalry be an ambush; the Minister must not fight them."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fled to his standard. Xue Nanyang said, "Send three hundred horsemen around by Mount Wan; do not meet them head-on.

sentences.zh: 兩軍相見，遂以麾下旁萬山而出其背，表裏夾擊，軍大敗，投水而死，殺獲殆盡。

translations.literal: When the two armies met, he then led his followers out by Mount Wan to take their rear; inner and outer struck together; the army was utterly defeated; they threw themselves into the water and died; those killed and captured were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies met, he slipped around Mount Wan and struck from the rear. Caught front and back, Pei's force was destroyed; men drowned themselves; few escaped.

sentences.zh: 及弟薦脫身北走，妻子並為瑱所擒，瑱甚厚撫之。

translations.literal: When his younger brother Jian escaped north, his wife and children were all captured by Zhen; Zhen treated them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's brother Jian fled north, but wife and children were taken; Zhen treated them kindly.

sentences.zh: 因抗表謝罪。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial asking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then memorialized asking leave to submit the case.

sentences.zh: 擒於申口，送至京師，長流費州，賜死於藍田故驛。

translations.literal: Ying was captured at Shenkou, sent to the capital, banished far to Feizhou, and granted death at the old Lantian post.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was taken at Shenkou, sent to court, banished to Feizhou, and ordered to die at the old Lantian post.

sentences.zh: 八月，瑱入朝謝罪，代宗特寵異之，遷兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，依前山南東道節度、觀察等使，代左僕射裴冕充山陵使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhen entered court to ask pardon; Daizong favored him exceptionally; he was moved to Minister of War, concurrent Chief Councilor, and kept as Shannan East military governor and observer, replacing the Left Vice Minister Pei Mian as director of the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhen came to court to answer charges. Daizong favored him, made him Minister of War and chief councilor, kept him on the Shannan East command, and set him over the imperial tombs in Pei Mian's place.

sentences.zh: 時中官驃騎大將軍程元振居中用事，發瑱言涉不順，王仲昇賊平來歸，證瑱與賊合，故令仲昇陷賊三年。

translations.literal: At that time the palace general Cheng Yuanzhen held power at court; he spread word that Zhen's speech touched on disloyalty; Wang Zhongsheng, when the rebels were pacified, returned and testified that Zhen had joined the rebels, so Yuanzhen caused Zhongsheng to be trapped with the rebels for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen then dominated court. He claimed Zhen's words smacked of treason; Wang Zhongsheng, returning after the rebellion, was made to testify that Zhen had colluded with the enemy, and Yuanzhen kept him in rebel hands for three years.

sentences.zh: 代宗含怒久之，因是下詔曰：

translations.literal: Daizong nursed anger long; because of this he issued an edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Daizong had long harbored wrath; he now issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，貴在於必書；

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals values what must be written;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that what must be recorded, must be recorded;

sentences.zh: 君臣之間，法存於無赦。

translations.literal: between ruler and minister the law stands in no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: between sovereign and subject the law knows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 沮勸式遵於前典，進退莫匪於至公，惡稔既彰，明罰難貸。

translations.literal: To discourage and encourage follows the former canon; advance and retreat are none but the utmost public justice; when wickedness is ripe and shown, clear punishment is hard to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment follow the ancient canon; promotion and dismissal must be utterly fair; when guilt is ripe, mercy is hard to grant.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、行兵部尚書、中書門下平章事、充山南東道節度觀察處置等使、上柱國、潁國公來瑱，謬當任用，素乏器能，亟歷班榮，累經節制。

translations.literal: Grand General with chief-minister insignia, acting Minister of War, Chief Councilor, Shannan East military governor and disposal commissioner, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Ying Lai Zhen—wrongly placed in office, by nature lacking capacity, repeatedly raised in court rank, repeatedly holding frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen, Grand General, acting Minister of War, chief councilor, Shannan East military governor, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Ying—unfit for office, devoid of talent, yet repeatedly honored and repeatedly given commands.

sentences.zh: 蒞職蔑聞於成績，登朝虛美於崇名。

translations.literal: In office he showed no achievement; in court he bore empty praise for lofty name.
translations.idiomatic: In post he achieved nothing; at court he bore only empty fame.

sentences.zh: 頃者分閫頒條，久淹江、漢。

translations.literal: Recently he divided a command and issued regulations, long detained on the Yangzi and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Lately he held the Yangzi and Han for years.

sentences.zh: 或頻徵不至，或移鎮遲留，實乖堂陛之儀，爰及干戈之忿。

translations.literal: Sometimes he was repeatedly summoned and did not come; sometimes he delayed in moving his command—truly contrary to the rites between hall and steps, and reaching to the wrath of arms.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored repeated summons or lingered when ordered to move—an affront to the court and an offense that called for arms.

sentences.zh: 朕以舊臣宿將，道在含弘，會其來庭，用甄後效。

translations.literal: We, because he was an old minister and veteran general, in the Way there is forbearance; when he came to court We would test his later conduct.
translations.idiomatic: We are an old servant of the throne; We meant to be forbearing and test him when he came to court.

sentences.zh: 超登宰輔，光拜夏卿，列在三臺，掩其一眚。

translations.literal: He was promoted above to chief minister, brightly appointed Summer Minister; he stood among the Three Terraces, covering one fault.
translations.idiomatic: Instead We raised him to chief minister and Minister of War, setting him among the Three Dukes while overlooking one fault.

sentences.zh: 山陵先遠，事委近臣，謀謨素闕於大猷，卜祝頗聞於私議。

translations.literal: The imperial tombs were far off; the affair was entrusted to a near minister; in counsel he always lacked great design; in divination and prayer much was heard of private discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The tombs lay far off; We entrusted them to a near minister—yet his counsel lacked grand design and private talk surrounded the rites.

sentences.zh: 實虧周慎，且間樞言，何以輔弼鼎司，儀刑簪紱？

translations.literal: Truly he fell short of thorough care, and moreover he obstructed the pivot's words—how can he assist the tripod vessel and be a model for the courtiers?
translations.idiomatic: He failed in grave duty, interfered with state counsel—how can such a man assist the throne or model the court?

sentences.zh: 據其所犯，合置殊科。

translations.literal: Judging his offenses, he deserves a special penalty.
translations.idiomatic: By his crimes he deserves extraordinary punishment.

sentences.zh: 以嘗侍軒闥，用存寬免之辜；

translations.literal: Because he once attended the imperial apartments, let the crime of death be spared;
translations.idiomatic: Because he once served near the throne, We spare his life;

sentences.zh: 緬範舊章，兼膺黜削之譴。

translations.literal: looking back to the old statutes, he shall also bear the censure of dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: by the old statutes he shall bear dismissal as well.

sentences.zh: 其身官爵，一切削除。

translations.literal: His person, office, and enfeoffment—all are struck off.
translations.idiomatic: His person, rank, and fief—all are abolished.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年正月，貶播州縣尉員外置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying, in the first month he was demoted to county captain of Bozhou, established extra statutorily.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoying, in the first month he was demoted to extra-statutory county captain of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賜死於鄠縣，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: The next day he was granted death at Huxian; his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was ordered to die at Huxian; his property was seized.

sentences.zh: 瑱之被刑也，門客四散，掩於坎中。

translations.literal: When Zhen suffered execution his retainers scattered; he was buried in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was executed his clients fled; he was cast into a shallow grave.

sentences.zh: 校書郎殷亮後至，獨哭於屍側，貨所乘驢以備棺衾，夜詣縣令長孫演以情告之，演義而從之。

translations.literal: The collator Yin Liang arrived later; he alone wept beside the corpse; he sold the donkey he rode to provide coffin and shroud; at night he went to the county magistrate Sun Yan and told him the story; Yan was moved by righteousness and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Collator Yin Liang came afterward and wept alone by the body; he sold his donkey for coffin and shroud, then at night persuaded Magistrate Sun Yan, who consented out of duty.

sentences.zh: 亮夜葬而祭，走歸京師。

translations.literal: Liang buried him by night and sacrificed, then fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang buried him by night, made offering, and fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗既悟元振之誣構，積其過而配流溱州。

translations.literal: Daizong, having realized Yuanzhen's false construction, accumulated his offenses and banished him to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong saw Yuanzhen's frame-up, he counted his crimes and banished him to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑱行軍司馬龐充統兵二千人赴河南，至汝州，聞瑱死，將士魚目等回兵襲襄州，左兵馬使李昭禦之，奔房州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhen's campaign secretary Pang Chong had commanded two thousand men to Henan; reaching Ruzhou, they heard Zhen was dead; the officers Yu Mu and others turned the army to strike Xiangzhou; the Left Army commander Li Zhao defended it; they fled to Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, campaign secretary Pang Chong had led two thousand men to Henan. At Ruzhou they heard Zhen was dead; officers led by Yu Mu turned back to strike Xiangzhou; Li Zhao held them off; they fled to Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭及薛南陽與右兵馬使梁崇義不葉相圖，為崇義所殺。

translations.literal: Zhao and Xue Nanyang could not get along with the Right Army commander Liang Chongyi; Chongyi killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao and Xue Nanyang quarreled with Right Army commander Liang Chongyi, who killed them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷授崇義節度使、兼御史中丞以代瑱。

translations.literal: The court appointed Chongyi military governor and concurrent Censor-in-Chief to replace Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Liang Chongyi military governor and concurrent Censor-in-Chief in Zhen's place.

sentences.zh: 崇義瑱立祠，四時拜饗，不居瑱廳及正堂視事，於東廂下構一小室而寢止，抗疏哀請收葬，優詔許之。

translations.literal: Chongyi erected a shrine to Zhen, offered sacrifice in the four seasons, did not occupy Zhen's hall or conduct affairs in the main hall, built a small room in the east wing to sleep in, and submitted a memorial pleading to recover the body; a gracious edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi built a shrine to Zhen, sacrificed each season, would not sit in Zhen's hall, slept in an east-wing room, and begged leave to recover the body—the court assented.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，追復官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde his office and enfeoffment were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 763 his rank and fief were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 周智光，本以騎射從軍，常有戎捷，自行間登偏裨。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang—Zhou Zhiguang originally followed the army through mounted archery; he often had frontier victories; from the ranks he rose to junior commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang first entered service as a mounted archer, won repeated frontier victories, and rose from the ranks to junior commander.

sentences.zh: 宦官魚朝恩為觀軍容使，鎮陜州，與之昵狎。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en was army-observing commissioner, garrisoned Shaanzhou, and was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chao'en, army-observing commissioner at Shaanzhou, favored him.

sentences.zh: 朝恩以扈從功，恩渥崇厚，奏請多允，屢於上前賞拔智光，累遷華州刺史、同華二州節度使及潼關防禦使，加檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫，

translations.literal: Chao'en for escort merit received thick favor; his requests were mostly granted; he repeatedly praised Zhiguang before the throne; Zhiguang was promoted repeatedly to Governor of Huazhou, military governor of Tong and Hua, defense commissioner of Tong Pass, and Acting Minister of Works with concurrent Censor-in-Chief,
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en's escort service won him favor; he praised Zhiguang again and again before the throne. Zhiguang rose to Governor of Hua, military governor of Tong and Hua, Tong Pass defender, and Acting Minister of Works with concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃、回紇、党項薔、渾、奴剌十餘萬眾寇奉天、醴泉等縣，智光邀戰，破於澄城，收駝馬軍資萬計，因逐賊至鄜州。

translations.literal: Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qi, Hun, and Nulaci—more than a hundred thousand in all—raided Fengtian, Liquan, and other counties; Zhiguang intercepted them and broke them at Chengcheng, seized camels, horses, and military stores by the tens of thousands, and pursued the bandits to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, and allied tribes—more than a hundred thousand—raided Fengtian and Liquan. Zhiguang met them at Chengcheng, took vast booty, and chased them to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 智光與杜冕不協，遂殺鄜州刺史張麟，坑杜冕家屬八十一人，焚坊州廬舍三千餘家。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was at odds with Du Mian; he thereupon killed the Binzhou prefect Zhang Lin, buried eighty-one members of Du Mian's household, and burned more than three thousand houses in Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At odds with Du Mian, he killed Binzhou prefect Zhang Lin, slaughtered eighty-one of Mian's kin, and burned three thousand dwellings in Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懼罪，召不赴命。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment, he was summoned but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, he ignored summons.

sentences.zh: 朝廷外示優容，俾杜冕使梁州，實避仇也。

translations.literal: Outwardly the court showed indulgence and sent Du Mian to Liangzhou—in fact to avoid the feud.
translations.idiomatic: The court outwardly indulged him while sending Du Mian to Liangzhou—really to escape revenge.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年十二月，智光專殺前虢州刺史、兼御史中孫龐充。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, in the twelfth month Zhiguang on his own authority killed the former Guozhou prefect and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Sun Pangchong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongtai, in the twelfth month Zhiguang murdered former Guozhou prefect Sun Pangchong on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 充方居缞绖，潛行，智光追而斬之。

translations.literal: Chong was in mourning garb and traveling in secret; Zhiguang pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Pangchong was in mourning and traveling secretly; Zhiguang chased him down and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 又劫諸節度使進奉貨物及轉運米二萬石，據州反。

translations.literal: He also plundered the tribute goods of the various military governors and twenty thousand shi of transport grain, and held the prefecture in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He robbed governors' tribute and twenty thousand shi of transport grain, and rebelled in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 智光自鄜坊專殺，朝廷患之，遂聚亡命不逞之徒，眾至數萬，縱其剽掠，以結其心。

translations.literal: Zhiguang since his murders in Bin and Fang had been a worry to the court; he then gathered lawless men on the run until they numbered in the tens of thousands, and let them plunder freely to bind their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bin-Fang massacres the court feared him; he gathered outlaws until they numbered tens of thousands and let them plunder freely to bind them to him.

sentences.zh: 初，與陜州節度使皇甫溫不協，監軍張志斌自陜入奏，智光館給禮慢，志斌責其不肅。

translations.literal: At first he was at odds with the Shaanzhou military governor Huangfu Wen; the army supervisor Zhang Zhibin entered court from Shaan; Zhiguang lodged and entertained him with rude ceremony; Zhibin reproached him for lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Shaanzhou governor Huangfu Wen. When army supervisor Zhang Zhibin came from Shaan to report, Zhiguang received him rudely; Zhibin rebuked his disrespect.

sentences.zh: 智光大怒曰：「僕固懷恩豈有反狀！

translations.literal: Zhiguang raged greatly and said, "Pugu Huai'en—how should he have had the appearance of rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang raged: "What sign of rebellion had Pugu Huai'en ever shown?

sentences.zh: 皆由爾鼠輩作福作威，懼死不敢入朝。

translations.literal: It is all because you rat fellows make blessings and make might, fearing death and not daring to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: It is you vermin who make fortune and power and dare not come to court for fear of death.

sentences.zh: 我本不反，今為爾作之。」

translations.literal: I originally did not rebel; now I rebel because of you."
translations.idiomatic: I was not going to rebel—but you have made me rebel.

sentences.zh: 因叱下斬之，臠其肉以飼從者。

translations.literal: He thereupon shouted to bring him down and behead him, and minced his flesh to feed his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhibin dragged down and killed, and minced his flesh to feed his followers.

sentences.zh: 時淮南節度使、檢校右僕射崔圓入覲，方物百萬，智光強留其半。

translations.literal: At that time the Huainan military governor and Acting Right Vice Minister Cui Yuan was entering audience; his local products were worth a million; Zhiguang forcibly kept half.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan governor Cui Yuan came to court with tribute worth a million, Zhiguang seized half by force.

sentences.zh: 舉選之士竦駭，或竊同州路以過，智光使部將邀斬於乾坑店，橫死者眾。

translations.literal: Candidates for office were terrified; some secretly took the Tongzhou road to pass; Zhiguang sent a subordinate to intercept and kill them at Qian'eng Inn; the dead lying across the road were many.
translations.idiomatic: Office-seekers were terrified; some slipped through by Tongzhou road; his officers cut them down at Qian'eng Inn until the dead lay thick.

sentences.zh: 優詔以智光為尚書左僕射，遣中使余元仙持告身以授之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict made Zhiguang Left Vice Minister of Works; the palace envoy Yu Yuanxian was sent with the commission to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict named him Left Vice Minister of Works; palace envoy Yu Yuanxian brought the commission.

sentences.zh: 智光受詔慢罵曰：「智光有數子，皆彎弓二百斤，有萬人敵，堪出將入相。

translations.literal: Zhiguang received the edict and reviled slowly: "Zhiguang has several sons; each can draw a two-hundred-jin bow; each is a match for ten thousand men, fit to go out as general and enter as minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang took the edict and sneered: "I have sons who bend two-hundred-jin bows, each a match for ten thousand—fit to be generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 只如挾天子令諸侯。

translations.literal: It is only like holding the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: It is only a matter of holding the Son of Heaven to command the lords.

sentences.zh: 天下只有周智光合作。」

translations.literal: Under Heaven only Zhou Zhiguang is fit to do it."
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven only Zhou Zhiguang is fit for that.

sentences.zh: 因歷數大臣之過。

translations.literal: He thereupon listed the faults of the great ministers one by one.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed the great ministers' faults one by one.

sentences.zh: 元仙股怵，智光增絹百匹遣之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian's thighs trembled; Zhiguang added a hundred bolts of silk and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian's legs shook; Zhiguang added a hundred bolts of silk and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 於州郭置生祠，俾將吏百姓祈禱。

translations.literal: Within the prefectural city he set up a living shrine and made generals, clerks, and commoners pray.
translations.idiomatic: He built a living shrine in the city and made officers and people worship there.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年正月，密詔關內河東副元帥、中書令郭子儀率兵討智光，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali, in the first month a secret edict ordered the Guannei and Hedong deputy commander-in-chief and Chief Councilor Guo Ziyi to lead troops to punish Zhiguang, with discretion to act as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dali, in the first month a secret edict ordered Guo Ziyi to march against Zhiguang with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 時同、華路絕，上召子儀女婿工部侍郎趙縱受口詔付子儀，縱裂帛寫詔置蠟丸中，遣家童間道達焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Tong-Hua road was cut; the Emperor summoned Ziyi's son-in-law, Vice Minister of Works Zhao Zong, to receive an oral edict for Ziyi; Zong wrote the edict on silk, placed it in a wax pill, and sent a household servant by a secret route to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tong-Hua road was cut; the Emperor had Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong take an oral edict written on silk in a wax ball and sent by a secret messenger.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉詔將出師，華州將士相顧攜貳。

translations.literal: Ziyi received the edict and was about to march; the Huazhou soldiers looked at one another with divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi prepared to march; the men of Hua looked at one another in doubt.

sentences.zh: 智光大將李漢惠自同州以其所管降子儀。

translations.literal: Zhiguang's great general Li Hanyu from Tongzhou led the troops under his command to surrender to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang's general Li Hanyu came over from Tongzhou with his command.

sentences.zh: 貶智光為澧州刺史，散官勛封如故。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was demoted to Governor of Li; his scattered-office rank and enfeoffment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was demoted to Governor of Li; honorary rank and fief stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 乃聽將一百人隨身，便路赴任，其所部將士官吏，一無所問。

translations.literal: He was permitted to take a hundred men in his personal following and go by the convenient route to his post; of the officers, soldiers, and clerks under his command, not one was questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He might take a hundred followers to his post by the shortest road; his officers and men were not punished.

sentences.zh: 乃以兵部侍郎張仲光為華州刺史、兼御史大夫、潼關防禦使；

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Minister of War Zhang Zhongguang was made Governor of Hua, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Tong Pass defense commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongguang was made Governor of Hua, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Tong Pass defender;

sentences.zh: 又以大理卿敬括為同州刺史、兼御史大夫、長春宮等使。

translations.literal: and Minister of Justice Jing Kuo was made Governor of Tong, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Changchun Palace commissioner, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Kuo was made Governor of Tong with concurrent Censor-in-Chief and Changchun Palace duties.

sentences.zh: 是日，智光為帳下將斬首，並子元耀、元幹等二人來獻。

translations.literal: That day Zhiguang was beheaded by a commander in his tent; his sons Yuanyao and Yuanqian and two others were brought in submission.
translations.idiomatic: That day his own officers beheaded him in camp; sons Yuanyao and Yuanqian were sent in.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，梟智光首於皇城之南街，二子腰斬以示眾。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Zhiguang's head was displayed at the south street of the Imperial City; the two sons were cut in two at the waist to show the masses.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao his head was displayed at the south gate of the palace; his two sons were cut in half at the waist before the crowd.

sentences.zh: 判官監察御史邵賁、都虞候蔣羅漢並伏誅，餘黨各以親疏準法定罪。

translations.literal: The aide Investigating Censor Shao Ben and the commandant of the guard Jiang Luohan were also executed; the rest of the party were sentenced by the closeness of kin according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Aide Shao Ben and guard officer Jiang Luohan were executed; the rest were sentenced by law according to kinship.

sentences.zh: 命有司具儀奏告太清宮、太廟、七陵。

translations.literal: Orders were given for the officials to prepare rites and report to the Supreme Ultimate Palace, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the seven tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered rites reported to the Supreme Ultimate Palace, the Ancestral Temple, and the seven imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李忠臣入觀，次潼關，聞智光阻兵，駐所部將往禦之。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was entering audience; he stopped at Tong Pass; hearing that Zhiguang blocked the army, he stationed his command to go and oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-Xi governor Li Zhongchen was then coming to court, halted at Tong Pass, and on hearing of the revolt moved to oppose Zhiguang.

sentences.zh: 及智光死，忠臣進兵入華州大掠，自赤水至潼關二百里間，畜產財物殆盡，官吏至有著紙衣或數日不食者。

translations.literal: When Zhiguang died, Zhongchen advanced into Huazhou and plundered on a great scale; from Chishui to Tong Pass for two hundred li livestock and goods were nearly exhausted; officials even wore paper clothes or went several days without food.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiguang's death Zhongchen marched into Hua and looted savagely. For two hundred li from Chishui to Tong Pass little property remained; some officials wore paper garments or starved for days.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：嘗讀《李陵傳》，戰敗不能死，屈節降虜庭，君不得為忠臣，母不得為孝子，每長嘆久之。

translations.literal: The historiographer says—the historiographer says: I have read the biography of Li Ling; defeated in battle he could not die, bent his integrity and surrendered in the barbarians' court; the lord could not be a loyal minister, the mother could not be a filial son—I have long sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: I have read the biography of Li Ling—defeated, unable to die, he submitted to the barbarians; neither loyal subject nor filial son—and I have long sighed at it.

sentences.zh: 炅收滍水敗眾，守南陽孤城，每蹈危機，竟效死節，料敵雖非其良將，事君不失為忠臣。

translations.literal: Jiong gathered the defeated masses at the Zhi River, held the lone city of Nanyang, at every step trod crisis, and in the end showed the integrity of death; in estimating the enemy he was not a good general, but in serving his lord he did not fail to be a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong rallied the broken army at the Zhi, held lonely Nanyang, faced death again and again, and in the end died faithful. He was no master of strategy, but he did not fail his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 浮躁無行，狂悖用兵，宜其死矣。

translations.literal: Frivolous and without conduct, wildly perverse in using arms—his death was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying was frivolous and reckless in war—small wonder he perished.

sentences.zh: 瑱善軍政，得士心，庶幾幹城禦侮者哉！

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled in military government and won the men's hearts—he was nearly a bulwark against insult!
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen knew how to command and held the men's hearts—he might have been a true shield of the realm.

sentences.zh: 始固名位，為裴巧言；

translations.literal: At first he clung to rank; Pei Ying's clever words;
translations.idiomatic: At first he clung to office because of Pei Ying's intrigues;

sentences.zh: 終歸朝廷，遭元振誣構。

translations.literal: in the end he returned to court and met Yuanzhen's false construction.
translations.idiomatic: in the end he answered the court and met Cheng Yuanzhen's frame-up.

sentences.zh: 賜死之辜匪辨，用刑之道不明。

translations.literal: The guilt of granted death was not distinguished; the Way of applying punishment was not clear.
translations.idiomatic: His guilt was never truly weighed; the law was not fairly applied.

sentences.zh: 致舊將立祠，門吏偷葬，出將入相，一至於斯，惜哉！

translations.literal: It led old generals to raise shrines and gate clerks to bury him in secret—from general to minister, to come to this—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Old officers raised shrines; clerks buried him in secret—a man who rose from general to minister, brought to this—alas!

sentences.zh: 智光狂悖，不足與論。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was wildly perverse—not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was mad with arrogance—not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：魯炅竭節，來瑱枉死。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Lu Jiong exhausted his integrity; Lai Zhen died wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Lu Jiong gave his all; Lai Zhen died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 裴兇人，智光逆子。

translations.literal: Pei Ying was a dangerous man; Zhiguang was a rebellious son.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ying was a villain; Zhiguang was a rebel.
